משום רבינו (49a.4) -- Rebbi, per Steinsaltz; the text says only 'our master'

props.gloss_en: R' Eliezer: whoever did not say 'a desirable, good and spacious land' in the blessing of the land, and the kingship of David's house in 'who builds Jerusalem', has not fulfilled his obligation
Nachum HaZaken: one must mention covenant in it [the blessing of the land]
R' Yosei: one must mention Torah in it
Pelimo: one must put covenant before Torah
Pelimo's reason: for this [the Torah] was given with three covenants
...and that [the covenant] was given with thirteen covenants
R' Abba: one must say thanks in it at the beginning and at the end
and one who reduces may not reduce below one [mention of thanks]
and whoever reduces below one is reprehensible
whoever closes the blessing of the land with 'who bequeaths lands' and 'who builds Jerusalem' with 'who saves Israel' is an ignoramus
and whoever does not say covenant and Torah in the blessing of the land, and the kingship of David's house in 'who builds Jerusalem', has not fulfilled his obligation

R' Il'a (R' Yaakov bar Acha, in the name of our master): whoever did not say covenant and Torah in the blessing of the land and the kingship of David's house in 'who builds Jerusalem' has not fulfilled his obligation
one says: 'who is good and does good' requires [mention of God's] kingship
the other says: it does not require [mention of] kingship
the one who says it requires kingship holds [that it is] rabbinic
the one who says it does not require kingship holds [that it is] Torah-law

supports.gloss_en: מסייע ליה לרבי אילעא -- the baraita's 'whoever does not say covenant and Torah... and David's kingship... has not fulfilled his obligation' is R' Il'a's dictum word for word
מאן דאמר צריכה מלכות קסבר דרבנן -- the one requiring kingship holds the blessing is rabbinic
ומאן דאמר אינה צריכה מלכות קסבר דאורייתא -- the one not requiring kingship holds the blessing is Torah-law
